name: quadrupole
description: A quadrupole cross-section: four round rods, alternating potential, solved in the plane normal to the axis. Present as the second, unrelated device of spec section 21 phase 5 — it shares no code with the mirror, only the three electrode primitives. Rod radius is set to 1.1468 times the inscribed radius, the ratio that best approximates a hyperbolic field with round rods. Near the axis the potential should go as (x^2 - y^2) and the restoring force should be linear, which is what makes it a mass filter once the potential is made to oscillate.

inscribedRadius.description: Distance from the axis to the nearest rod surface, conventionally r0.

rodRatio.description: Rod radius as a multiple of the inscribed radius. 1.1468 is the classical optimum for round rods: the value that cancels the leading non-ideal multipole, the 12-pole. Bounded so an optimiser can search for it rather than being told it.

rodPotential.description: Applied to the x-pair; the y-pair takes its negative.

housingClearance.description: Distance from a rod centre to the grounded wall, beyond the rod radius, as a multiple of the rod radius. The classical rod ratio assumes no housing at all, so this is the parameter that says how far from that assumption a given design sits.

cellsPerRadius.description: Grid cells across the inscribed radius.

probeFraction.description: How far out the probe ion crosses the aperture, as a fraction of r0. It has to be a fraction rather than a length: this template exists to have its inscribed radius changed, and a placement in bare millimetres that is comfortably inside the aperture at one radius sits exactly on a rod at another. That is what happened here - the source was written as -4 mm, which is 0.8 r0 at the shipped 5 mm and precisely on the metal at 4 mm, and neither validate nor solve objected.
